title: Call Web API from jQuery in ASP.NET Core
description: Use jQuery AJAX to consume all CRUD operations of an ASP.NET Core Web API, including DELETE with dynamic events and file upload.

data.text: Why jQuery for API Calls?

**jQuery** is a popular JavaScript library that simplifies DOM manipulation and AJAX calls. Its `$.ajax()` method provides a clean, chainable syntax for making HTTP requests, handling success and error callbacks, and updating the page — all with less code than raw XHR.

data.title: jQuery AJAX in a nutshell
data.text: The $.ajax() method accepts a configuration object with url, type, contentType, data, success, and error keys. jQuery handles the XMLHttpRequest creation and state tracking for you.
jQuery AJAX Request Flow

data.text: PUT — Fully Replace a Reservation

For **PUT** the API expects form data (`[FromForm]`). Build a `FormData` object, set `processData: false` and `contentType: false` in the jQuery AJAX config so jQuery does not interfere with the multipart encoding.

data.text: PATCH — Partially Update a Reservation
The PATCH action requires a JSON Patch document. Build it with `JSON.stringify()` and set the Content-Type to `application/json-patch+json`.

data.title: jQuery — PATCH specific fields
data.content: Send only the fields that need to change.
data.code:
<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {
        const params = new URL(document.location).searchParams;
        const id = params.get("id");

        function GetReservation() {
            $.ajax({
                url: `https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/${id}`,
                type: "get",
                contentType: "application/json",
                success: function (result) {
                    $("#Id").val(result["id"]);
                    $("#Name").val(result["name"]);
                    $("#StartLocation").val(result["startLocation"]);
                },
                error: function (xhr) { console.log(xhr); }
            });
        }
        GetReservation();

        $("#UpdateButton").click(function () {
            const id = new URL(document.location).searchParams.get("id");
            $.ajax({
                url: `https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/${id}`,
                type: "patch",
                contentType: "application/json-patch+json",
                data: JSON.stringify([
                    { op: "replace", path: "Name", value: $("#Name").val() },
                    { op: "replace", path: "StartLocation", value: $("#StartLocation").val() }
                ]),
                success: function () { window.location.href = "AllReservation.html"; },
                error: function (xhr) { console.log(xhr); }
            });
        });
    });
</script>

jQuery AJAX handles file uploads through `FormData`. Set `processData: false` and `contentType: false` so jQuery sends the multipart data as-is.

data.title: jQuery — Upload file to Web API
data.content: Append file to FormData and POST with jQuery AJAX.
data.code:
<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {
        $("#AddButton").click(function () {
            const formData = new FormData();
            formData.append("file", $("#File")[0].files[0]);

            $.ajax({
                url: "https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/UploadFile",
                type: "post",
                data: formData,
                processData: false,
                contentType: false,
                success: function (result) {
                    $("#fileImg").attr("src", result);
                    $("#fileDiv").show();
                },
                error: function (xhr) { console.log(xhr); }
            });
        });
    });
</script>

data.title: Convert XHR Pages to jQuery
data.description: Take the XHR-based pages you built in the previous lesson and rewrite them using jQuery $.ajax() instead of XMLHttpRequest.
steps: Include jQuery via CDN in each page.
Replace each XMLHttpRequest block with a $.ajax() call.
Use $("#id").val() to read inputs and $("<tag>") to create elements.
Use delegated events ($("table").on("click", ...)) for dynamically created delete icons.
Set processData: false and contentType: false for FormData requests.
data.expectedOutcome: Five working jQuery pages (all, get-by-id, add, update, patch) that behave identically to the XHR versions but use jQuery syntax throughout.

items.text: jQuery library is loaded via CDN before any script that uses $.
GET call uses type: 'get' and populates the table in the success callback.
DELETE uses delegated event on the table.
POST stringifies the data object and sets contentType: 'application/json'.
PUT uses FormData with processData: false and contentType: false.
File upload uses FormData with processData: false and contentType: false.

items.question: What does contentType: false do?
items.answer: It tells jQuery not to set the Content-Type header. When using FormData, jQuery cannot determine the correct multipart boundary string, so it should not set the header — the browser sets it automatically with the correct boundary.

items.question: What does processData: false do?
items.answer: It prevents jQuery from converting the FormData object into a query string. FormData must be sent as-is to preserve the multipart encoding.

items.question: Why use a delegated event for delete?
items.answer: Delete icons are created dynamically after the AJAX call. A direct .click() binding only works for elements existing at bind time. Delegated events on a static ancestor catch events from all current and future matching descendants.

items.question: Is jQuery still relevant in 2026?
items.answer: jQuery is less common in new greenfield projects, but many enterprise and legacy applications still use it. Understanding jQuery AJAX is also a solid foundation for understanding the underlying XMLHttpRequest pattern.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: jQuery $.ajax() wraps XMLHttpRequest with a cleaner, callback-based API.
Use JSON.stringify() with contentType: 'application/json' for JSON bodies.
Use FormData with processData: false and contentType: false for multipart uploads.
Delegated events ($(parent).on(event, selector, handler)) handle dynamically created elements.
PATCH requires contentType: 'application/json-patch+json' and a JSON Patch document body.
data.takeaway: You can now consume any ASP.NET Core Web API from jQuery, handling every CRUD operation and file uploads.
